items.informal_name: Degree Bound in Coefficients via Fin(n+1) Equivalence
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ} (p : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R) (j : Fin n) (i : ℕ),
  MvPolynomial.degreeOf j (((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) p).coeff i) ≤ MvPolynomial.degreeOf j.succ p
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ p $ over $ \text{Fin}(n+1) $, any $ j \in \text{Fin}(n) $, and any natural number $ i $, the degree of the variable $ j $ in the $ i $-th coefficient of the polynomial obtained by applying the algebra equivalence $ \text{finSuccEquiv} $ to $ p $ is less than or equal to the degree of the variable $ j.\text{succ} $ in $ p $. This equivalence maps variables indexed by $ \text{Fin}(n+1) $ to a polynomial ring in one variable with coefficients in multivariate polynomials over $ \text{Fin}(n) $, preserving algebraic structure while bounding variable degrees in coefficients.

items.informal_name: Total Degree Inequality for Coefficients in Fin(n+1) Polynomial Equivalence
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R) (i : ℕ),
  ((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) f).coeff i ≠ 0 →
    (((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) f).coeff i).totalDegree + i ≤ f.totalDegree
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ f $ over $ \text{Fin}(n+1) $ with coefficients in a commutative semiring $ R $, and for any natural number $ i $ such that the $ i $-th coefficient of the algebra equivalence $ \text{finSuccEquiv}(R, n, f) $ is nonzero, the total degree of this coefficient polynomial plus $ i $ is less than or equal to the total degree of $ f $. This reflects the degree preservation property under the variable-renaming equivalence between $ R[\text{Fin}(n+1)] $ and $ R[\text{Fin}(n)][X] $.

items.informal_name: Degree in a Variable is Bounded by Total Degree
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : MvPolynomial σ R) (i : σ),
  MvPolynomial.degreeOf i f ≤ f.totalDegree
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ f $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, and for any variable $ i \in \sigma $, the degree of $ f $ in $ i $ is less than or equal to the total degree of $ f $. That is, $ \deg_i(f) \leq \deg(f) $, where $ \deg_i(f) $ denotes the maximum exponent of $ i $ in any monomial of $ f $, and $ \deg(f) $ is the maximum sum of exponents in any monomial of $ f $.

items.informal_name: Monomial Exponent Bounded by Total Degree in Multivariate Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (i : σ) {f : MvPolynomial σ R} {m : σ →₀ ℕ},
  m ∈ f.support → m i ≤ MvPolynomial.degreeOf i f
items.informal_description: For any variable $i$ in $\sigma$, multivariate polynomial $f \in R[\sigma]$, and monomial $m$ in the support of $f$ (i.e., with nonzero coefficient), the exponent of $i$ in $m$ satisfies $m_i \leq \deg_i(f)$, where $\deg_i(f)$ denotes the total degree of $f$ in variable $i$ (sum of exponents of $i$ across all monomials in $f$).

items.informal_name: Total Degree Submodule is Contained in Individual Degree Submodule
items.type:
∀ (σ : Type u) (R : Type v) [inst : CommSemiring R] (m : ℕ),
  MvPolynomial.restrictTotalDegree σ R m ≤ MvPolynomial.restrictDegree σ R m
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $ and type $ \sigma $, the submodule of multivariate polynomials over $ R $ with total degree at most $ m $ is contained within the submodule of polynomials where each variable's exponent is at most $ m $. This holds because a monomial's total degree being bounded by $ m $ implies each individual exponent is also bounded by $ m $.
